classifications.COPY_OK: Direct adaptation may be possible after exact-file license review and tests.
classifications.VENDOR_OR_WRAP: Use through a stable boundary or vendor a narrow pinned component.
classifications.PORT_ALGORITHM: Reimplement/port a bounded algorithm with new tests.
classifications.IDEAS_ONLY: Transfer architecture or behavior specification; do not copy source.
classifications.BENCHMARK_ONLY: Use for experiments and comparisons, not production runtime.
classifications.LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED: No direct reuse until licensing is resolved.

projects.observed: Implements Total War PackFile decoding/encoding, dependency metadata, lazy loading, compression, DB/Loc handling and diagnostics. The pack module also contains explicit handling hooks for siege-AI map hints.
projects.reuse: Use as the authoritative pack/schema/diagnostic foundation or invoke its headless/server capabilities. Do not write a new pack parser or table editor.
projects.risks: Large Rust/Qt codebase; pin schema and game build; keep runtime AI independent from the authoring tool.

projects.observed: Versioned schema and patch data used to decode Total War database tables.
projects.reuse: Pin as a submodule/artifact and record the schema revision used for every generated pack and benchmark.
projects.risks: Schemas can lag a new game patch; build a compatibility gate rather than silently generating with stale definitions.

projects.observed: Provides TypeScript-to-Lua structure, logging, saved-value wrappers, first-tick helpers, engine-synchronized random helpers, timer/listener abstractions and typed campaign code organization.
projects.reuse: Strong starting toolchain for compile-time safety. Fork minimally, add generated WH3 interface declarations, strict lint rules, deterministic-random guardrails and testable pure-domain modules.
projects.risks: Types are incomplete and transpilation adds another failure layer. Never let wrapper types imply an engine capability that has not been tested.

projects.project: Knights of the Round Belly — TypeScript
projects.observed: A real mod built on the TypeScript approach, with namespaced modules, typed data maps, event listeners, faction/region data, AI-specific branches and campaign mutations.
projects.reuse: Use as evidence that the toolchain can support a nontrivial campaign mod and as a corpus for build/layout conventions.
projects.risks: Content-specific global data and large monolithic files are examples to improve, not copy. Verify license before reuse.

projects.observed: Manager with mandatory module contracts, default settings, persistent staged state, MCT integration, dynamic file discovery, protected loading with pcall, per-module validation and error isolation.
projects.reuse: Port the plugin contract, module validation, staged lifecycle, save wrapper and fail-soft loading into faction doctrines, strategic policies and scenario modules.
projects.risks: No repository LICENSE found in this pass; concepts are safe to study, direct copying requires owner/license review.

projects.observed: Uses first-tick registration, event-specific listeners, model traversal, saved counters and faction-specific objective evaluators.
projects.reuse: Adapt its clean event-to-check-to-state-update shape for strategic objective evaluators and faction policy modules.
projects.risks: It is an objective framework, not a general AI. Avoid conflating mission completion checks with planning.

projects.observed: At FactionTurnStart, inspects AI armies, caches a recruitment-cost pool, detects policy violations, replaces units and reimburses the faction. It demonstrates indirect control around CA's opaque planner.
projects.reuse: Use its bounded policy-enforcement pattern for composition constraints, emergency corrections and post-planner safeguards.
projects.risks: One path uses math.random rather than the engine RNG; audit determinism before reuse. Replacing units is corrective intervention, not genuine strategic reasoning.

projects.observed: Parses packs, displays DB data, computes load-order overwrite/compatibility information and has a testable Electron/TypeScript codebase.
projects.reuse: Reuse or invoke its conflict-analysis ideas to create CI that reports table/script collisions against a benchmark mod list.
projects.risks: Desktop application concerns should not leak into runtime. Prefer a small library/CLI boundary or generated compatibility report.

source_paths: script object lifecycle and event-handler maps
projects.observed: Open-source in-game scripting console for earlier Total War titles, using protected dynamic script execution and lifecycle-oriented script objects.
projects.reuse: Study its interactive console, hot-run workflow, command history, pcall isolation and start/stop script lifecycle for a WH3 developer harness.
projects.risks: Not a WH3 implementation and GPL-3.0. Reimplement behavior cleanly unless the whole relevant component is license-compatible.

projects.project: Total War Simulator / Total War: AI
projects.observed: Unity battle simulator with unit paths, formation-slot assignment, combat-state transitions, melee/ranged/cavalry mechanics and an AI-research goal.
projects.reuse: Fork as a starting surrogate battle lab or extract formation/assignment experiments. Use it to test algorithms before expensive WH3 runs.
projects.risks: Unity 2019-era simplified physics and mechanics differ greatly from WH3. It must be calibrated against telemetry and never treated as a faithful forward model without validation.

projects.observed: Separates state, legal action generation, action assignment, conditions/effects and state advancement; explicitly supports reduced forward models for search/training.
projects.reuse: Best reference for a project-owned abstract campaign/battle forward model and action-space contract used by search and offline evaluation.
projects.risks: C++ research environment is not a WH3 runtime dependency. Port abstractions and test against real telemetry.

projects.observed: Data-driven bot modules, squad role assignment, staggered update intervals, target filters, visibility checks, path-aware target reachability, attack/defense states and saveable bot data.
projects.reuse: Adopt the modular bot-manager shape, update staggering, explicit squad roles, state machines and debug-state visibility.
projects.risks: GPL and engine-specific C#. Use patterns unless project licensing deliberately accommodates direct reuse.

projects.observed: Thin top-level commander delegates to strategy, production, combat, scouting and squad systems; includes build-order search and combat simulation components.
projects.reuse: Use its manager boundaries and explicit command pipeline as a strong template for strategic, operational and tactical decomposition.
projects.risks: StarCraft/BWAPI assumptions and high-APM economy differ from Total War. Port interfaces and algorithms selectively.

projects.observed: Normalizes game observations into a bot API, separates public and internal lifecycle logic, caches expensive queries, and supports reproducible example agents.
projects.reuse: Model the WH3 adapter and immutable snapshot API after this separation: engine details at the edge, clean domain queries and orders in the core.
projects.risks: SC2 has a supported external API; WH3 does not expose an equivalent full observation/order protocol.

projects.observed: Purpose-built compact RTS research environment with hard-coded rush policies, minimax/Monte Carlo/MCTS variants, action abstraction and explicit computation budgets.
projects.reuse: Use as a controlled algorithm bake-off environment and a reference for budgeted search, action abstraction and tournament evaluation.
projects.risks: Tiny grid RTS dynamics are far removed from WH3 formations, morale, terrain, spells and campaign state.

projects.observed: Defines structured observation planes, multi-discrete actions, legal-action masking, vectorized environments and affordable full-game RTS RL experiments.
projects.reuse: Borrow action-mask, curriculum, vector-evaluation and reproducible-training ideas for the offline surrogate—not for direct WH3 runtime control.
projects.risks: Reward hacking, simulator mismatch and large validation burden. Do not make RL a prerequisite for the first competent release.

projects.observed: A dedicated AI subsystem with gateway boundary, goal/resource logic and mock-based tests for campaign-map decisions.
projects.reuse: Study danger assessment, goal decomposition, hero/army tasking and the use of mocks to test strategic logic without launching the game.
projects.risks: Heroes III rules and GPL licensing. Transfer architecture, not code.

projects.observed: Persistent AI state, priority calculation, diplomacy, research/production, exploration, fleet mission assignment, order generation and explicit savegame codecs.
projects.reuse: Excellent model for campaign-phase decomposition, persisted strategic state and separating priority formation from order emission.
projects.risks: Turn-based space-4X abstractions and GPL; patterns only.

projects.observed: Candidate actions evaluate applicability and score before execution; Lua extension and focused micro-AIs support regroup, protect and recruiting behavior.
projects.reuse: Adopt candidate-action/utility evaluation as the default explainable decision kernel and use focused micro-policies rather than one giant planner.
projects.risks: Hex turn-based combat and GPL. Transfer design and tests, not implementation.

projects.observed: Production-game AI focused on construction, resources, logistics, expansion and military interaction under long time horizons.
projects.reuse: Mine for bottleneck detection, construction prioritization, resource reservation and periodic work scheduling relevant to WH3 economy/building policy.
projects.risks: Economic network mechanics are unlike WH3 province slots; GPL.

projects.observed: Script-level skirmish AI split into event handling, build/economy logic and combat behavior.
projects.reuse: Useful analogue for a Lua/JS event-driven AI living above an engine-owned simulation, particularly scheduling and modular script layout.
projects.risks: Full skirmish scripting API is richer than WH3’s general campaign/battle surfaces; GPL.

projects.observed: Persistent theater object, AI commander, asset/template systems, ticket/resource system, settings and UI around a Lua-scripted military campaign.
projects.reuse: Strong conceptual match for WH3 theaters, strategic objectives, asset assignment and bounded resource accounting.
projects.risks: DCS mission API and real-time theater assumptions differ; LGPL obligations require care if code is ported.

projects.observed: Tested HTN decomposition with explicit contexts, conditions, effects, planner state and domain builders.
projects.reuse: Port a minimal deterministic HTN kernel only for decisions that genuinely benefit from multi-step decomposition, such as invasion preparation or siege continuation.
projects.risks: Do not use HTN for every choice. Runtime is C#, so Lua port and property tests are required.

projects.observed: Factory-registered nodes, typed ports/blackboards, runtime tree loading, reactive/asynchronous execution and logging examples.
projects.reuse: Borrow node contracts, blackboard typing, cancellation and trace tooling for tactical execution plans; implement a small Lua-native subset.
projects.risks: A full C++ library cannot run in normal WH3 Lua. Avoid recreating a huge generic editor before proving need.

projects.project: Beyond All Reason — headless testing corpus
projects.observed: Repository includes headless smoke scripts, deterministic start scripts and scenario content used to exercise AI/game behavior.
projects.reuse: Emulate the scenario-as-code and smoke-test workflow even though WH3 itself may require UI-driven runs.
projects.risks: AI implementation is spread across Spring/BAR components; verify component licenses and canonical AI upstream before any copying.
